fn.ACCRINT: Interest accrued on a security that pays periodic interest.
fn.ACCRINTM: Interest accrued on a security that pays at maturity.
fn.ADDRESS: A cell address as text; choose absolute or relative references, A1 or R1C1 notation, and an optional sheet.
fn.AGGREGATE: SUBTOTAL with more functions and options to skip hidden rows (1) and errors (2); 14-19 take k.
fn.AI: Asks Puter AI a question, optionally about a range of data; the answer fills the cell (#BUSY! while it thinks).
fn.AMORDEGRC: Declining-balance depreciation for an accounting period (French system), with a coefficient by asset life.
fn.AMORLINC: Linear depreciation of an asset for an accounting period (French system), prorated in the first period.
fn.AND: TRUE when every argument is true.
fn.ARABIC: Roman numerals back to a number.
fn.AREAS: How many areas a reference has, as in (A1:B2,D4).
fn.ARRAYTOTEXT: An array as text; format 1 keeps braces and quotes.
fn.ARRAY_CONSTRAIN: The top-left part of an array.
fn.ASC: Full-width (double-byte) letters as half-width ones, under a double-byte language.
fn.ATAN2: Angle of a point, in radians.
fn.AVEDEV: Average absolute deviation from the mean.
fn.AVERAGEA: Average, counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.
fn.AVERAGEIF: Average of cells that meet a condition.
fn.AVERAGEIFS: Average of cells meeting several conditions.
fn.BAHTTEXT: A number in Thai words, as baht and satang.
fn.BASE: A number as text in another base.
fn.BESSELI: Modified Bessel function of the first kind, order n.
fn.BESSELJ: Bessel function of the first kind, order n.
fn.BESSELK: Modified Bessel function of the second kind, order n.
fn.BESSELY: Bessel function of the second kind (Weber), order n.
fn.BETADIST: Beta cumulative distribution (older name of BETA.DIST).
fn.BETAINV: Inverse of the beta cumulative distribution (older name of BETA.INV).
fn.BETA_DIST: Beta distribution, optionally rescaled to [A, B].
fn.BETA_INV: Inverse of the beta cumulative distribution.
fn.BINOM_DIST_RANGE: Probability of a count of successes between two bounds.
fn.BINOM_INV: Smallest count of successes whose cumulative probability reaches alpha.
fn.BITLSHIFT: A number shifted left by some bits.
fn.BITRSHIFT: A number shifted right by some bits.
fn.BITXOR: Bitwise exclusive OR of two numbers.
fn.BYCOL: Applies a LAMBDA to each column.
fn.BYROW: Applies a LAMBDA to each row.
fn.CEILING: Rounds up to a multiple of significance.
fn.CEILING_MATH: Rounds up to a multiple; mode 1 rounds negatives away from zero.
fn.CEILING_PRECISE: Rounds up to a multiple, whatever the sign of significance.
fn.CELL: Information about a cell: its "address", "row", "col", "contents", "type", "format", "prefix", "protect" or "width".
fn.CHAR: The character with a code number.
fn.CHIDIST: Right-tailed chi-squared distribution (older name of CHISQ.DIST.RT).
fn.CHIINV: Inverse of the right-tailed chi-squared distribution (older name of CHISQ.INV.RT).
fn.CHISQ_INV: Inverse of the left-tailed chi-squared distribution.
fn.CHISQ_INV_RT: Inverse of the right-tailed chi-squared distribution.
fn.CHISQ_TEST: Probability from a chi-squared test of independence.
fn.CHITEST: Chi-squared test of independence (older name of CHISQ.TEST).
fn.CHOOSECOLS: Chosen columns of a range; spills.
fn.CHOOSEROWS: Chosen rows of a range; spills.
fn.CODE: Code number of the first character.
fn.COLUMNS: How many columns a range or array has.
fn.COMPLEX: A complex number "a+bi" from its parts.
fn.CONCATENATE: Joins text; arrays join element by element.
fn.CONFIDENCE: Half-width of a confidence interval for a mean, normal distribution (older name of CONFIDENCE.NORM).
fn.CONFIDENCE_NORM: Half-width of a confidence interval for a mean.
fn.CONFIDENCE_T: Half-width of a confidence interval for a mean, Student t distribution.
fn.CONVERT: Converts between units: "mi" to "km", "lbm" to "kg", "F" to "C", ...
fn.COS: Cosine of an angle in radians.
fn.COT: Cotangent of an angle in radians.
fn.COUNTA: How many cells are not empty.
fn.COUNTIF: Counts cells that meet a condition.
fn.COUNTUNIQUEIFS: Distinct values in a range whose rows meet the criteria.
fn.COUPDAYBS: Days from the start of the coupon period to settlement.
fn.COUPDAYS: Days in the coupon period that contains settlement.
fn.COUPDAYSNC: Days from settlement to the next coupon date.
fn.COUPNCD: The first coupon date after settlement.
fn.COUPNUM: Coupons payable between settlement and maturity.
fn.COUPPCD: The coupon date on or before settlement.
fn.CRITBINOM: Smallest count of successes whose cumulative probability reaches alpha (older name of BINOM.INV).
fn.CSC: Cosecant of an angle in radians.
fn.CUBEKPIMEMBER: A key performance indicator property from a cube; needs a data connection (#N/A).
fn.CUBEMEMBER: A member or tuple from an OLAP cube; needs a data connection (#N/A).
fn.CUBEMEMBERPROPERTY: A property of a cube member; needs a data connection (#N/A).
fn.CUBERANKEDMEMBER: The nth member of a cube set; needs a data connection (#N/A).
fn.CUBESET: A set of cube members; needs a data connection (#N/A).
fn.CUBESETCOUNT: The number of items in a cube set; needs a data connection (#N/A).
fn.CUBEVALUE: An aggregated value from an OLAP cube; needs a data connection (#N/A).
fn.DATEVALUE: Turns date text into a date.
fn.DAVERAGE: Average of a column over matching rows.
fn.DAYS360: Days between dates on a 360-day year.
fn.DBCS: Half-width (single-byte) letters as full-width ones, under a double-byte language.
fn.DCOUNT: How many matching rows hold a number in the column.
fn.DCOUNTA: How many matching rows are not empty in the column.
fn.DECIMAL: Text in a base back to a number.
fn.DELTA: 1 when two numbers are equal, else 0.
fn.DETECTLANGUAGE: The two-letter code of the language a text is written in, from Puter AI.
fn.DEVSQ: Sum of squared deviations from the mean.
fn.DGET: The single value that matches; #NUM! when several do.
fn.DMAX: Largest value of a column over matching rows.
fn.DMIN: Smallest value of a column over matching rows.
fn.DOLLAR: Formats a number as currency text.
fn.DOLLARDE: A fractional price (like 1.02 for 1 2/16) as a decimal.
fn.DOLLARFR: A decimal price as a fractional one.
fn.DPRODUCT: Product of a column over matching rows.
fn.DROP: Everything but the first (or last) rows and columns.
fn.DSTDEV: Sample standard deviation over matching rows.
fn.DSTDEVP: Population standard deviation over matching rows.
fn.DSUM: Sum of a column over the rows that match a criteria table.
fn.DURATION: Macaulay duration of a bond, in years.
fn.ENCODEURL: Escapes text for use in a URL.
fn.EPOCHTODATE: A Unix timestamp (seconds, 2 = ms, 3 = µs) as a date.
fn.EQ: TRUE when the values are equal (the = operator).
fn.ERF: Error function integrated between the limits.
fn.ERF_PRECISE: Error function integrated from 0 to x.
fn.ERROR_TYPE: A number for each kind of error.
fn.EVEN: Rounds up to an even integer.
fn.EXACT: TRUE when two texts are the same, case included.
fn.EXPAND: Grows an array, padding the new cells.
fn.FDIST: Right-tailed F distribution (older name of F.DIST.RT).
fn.FILTER: Rows (or columns) where every condition is TRUE; spills.
fn.FILTERXML: Values picked from XML text by an XPath expression, spilled down.
fn.FINDB: Position of text, case-sensitive (the same as FIND here).
fn.FINV: Inverse of the right-tailed F distribution (older name of F.INV.RT).
fn.FIXED: Formats a number with fixed decimals as text.
fn.FLATTEN: Every value in one column; spills.
fn.FLOOR: Rounds down to a multiple of significance.
fn.FLOOR_MATH: Rounds down to a multiple; mode 1 rounds negatives toward zero.
fn.FLOOR_PRECISE: Rounds down to a multiple, whatever the sign of significance.
fn.FORECAST: Predicts y for x along the best-fit line.
fn.FORECAST_ETS: Forecasts a future value by exponential triple smoothing.
fn.FORECAST_ETS_CONFINT: Confidence interval of the forecast at the target date.
fn.FORECAST_ETS_SEASONALITY: Length of the repeating pattern detected in the values.
fn.FORECAST_ETS_STAT: A statistic of the exponential smoothing forecast.
fn.FORECAST_LINEAR: Predicts y for x along the best-fit line.
fn.FORMULATEXT: The formula in a cell, as text.
fn.FREQUENCY: How many values fall into each bin.
fn.FTEST: Two-tailed probability that two samples have different variances (older name of F.TEST).
fn.FVSCHEDULE: Future value under a schedule of rates.
fn.F_INV: Inverse of the left-tailed F distribution.
fn.F_INV_RT: Inverse of the right-tailed F distribution.
fn.F_TEST: Two-tailed probability that two samples have different variances.
fn.GAMMAINV: Inverse of the gamma cumulative distribution (older name of GAMMA.INV).
fn.GAMMALN: Natural logarithm of the gamma function.
fn.GAMMALN_PRECISE: Natural logarithm of the gamma function.
fn.GAMMA_INV: Inverse of the gamma cumulative distribution.
fn.GAUSS: Probability a standard normal value falls between 0 and z.
fn.GESTEP: 1 when a number is at least the step, else 0.
fn.GETPIVOTDATA: A value from a PivotTable: the data field, narrowed by field and item pairs (the grand total when none are given).
fn.GOOGLETRANSLATE: Translates text with Puter AI (the Sheets name for TRANSLATE).
fn.GROUPBY: Groups rows by one or more fields and summarizes the values with a function named without parentheses (SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, ...) or a LAMBDA; totals, subtotals, sorting, and a filter are optional.
fn.GROWTH: Values along the fitted exponential curve.
fn.HLOOKUP: Looks across the first row, returns from another.
fn.HOUR: The hour of a time, 0 to 23.
fn.HYPGEOM_DIST: Hypergeometric distribution: successes in a sample drawn without replacement.
fn.IF: One value or another depending on a test.
fn.IFERROR: A fallback when a value is an error.
fn.IFNA: A fallback when a value is #N/A.
fn.IFS: First value whose condition is true.
fn.IMAGE: Shows a picture in the cell: mode 1 fits, 2 stretches, 3 keeps the original size. With alt text second, sizing 0 fits, 1 fills, 2 keeps the original size.
fn.IMAGINARY: Imaginary part of a complex number.
fn.IMARGUMENT: Argument (angle in radians) of a complex number.
fn.IMCOSH: Hyperbolic cosine of a complex number.
fn.IMCSCH: Hyperbolic cosecant of a complex number.
fn.IMEXP: e raised to a complex power.
fn.IMLN: Natural logarithm of a complex number.
fn.IMLOG10: Base-10 logarithm of a complex number.
fn.IMLOG2: Base-2 logarithm of a complex number.
fn.IMPORTDATA: A CSV or TSV file from a web address, spilled into place; #BUSY! while it downloads.
fn.IMPORTHTML: The nth table or list on a web page, spilled into place; #BUSY! while it downloads.
fn.IMPORTRANGE: Cells from another spreadsheet on your Puter drive ("Budget" or a path, then "Sheet1!A1:B10"); #BUSY! while it loads.
fn.IMPORTXML: Nodes picked by an XPath query from an XML or HTML document, one per row; #BUSY! while it downloads.
fn.IMPOWER: A complex number raised to a power.
fn.IMREAL: Real part of a complex number.
fn.IMSECH: Hyperbolic secant of a complex number.
fn.IMSINH: Hyperbolic sine of a complex number.
fn.IMSQRT: Square root of a complex number.
fn.INDEX: The value at a position in a range.
fn.INDIRECT: The cell or range a text address names. Use FALSE for R1C1 notation; TRUE or omitted uses A1.
fn.INTERCEPT: Where the best-fit line crosses the y axis.
fn.INTRATE: Interest rate of a fully invested security.
fn.ISBETWEEN: TRUE when a value lies between two others.
fn.ISEMAIL: TRUE for text that looks like an email address.
fn.ISFORMULA: TRUE when the cell holds a formula.
fn.ISNONTEXT: TRUE when a value is not text.
fn.ISOMITTED: TRUE when an optional LAMBDA parameter, written [name], was left out by the caller.
fn.ISO_CEILING: Rounds up to a multiple, whatever the sign of significance.
fn.ISPMT: Interest for a period of an even-principal loan.
fn.ISREF: TRUE when the argument is a reference.
fn.ISURL: TRUE for text that looks like a web address.
fn.JIS: Half-width (single-byte) letters as full-width ones (the same as DBCS).
fn.LAMBDA: A custom function, for MAP, REDUCE, BYROW, or a LET name.
fn.LEFTB: Characters from the start (the same as LEFT here).
fn.LENB: Number of characters (the same as LEN here).
fn.LET: Names intermediate values, then computes a result with them.
fn.LINEST: Slope and intercept of the least-squares line, with its statistics when asked.
fn.LOG: Logarithm in a base, 10 when left out.
fn.LOGEST: Base and constant of the fitted exponential curve, with its statistics when asked.
fn.LOGINV: Inverse of the lognormal cumulative distribution (older name of LOGNORM.INV).
fn.LOGNORMDIST: Lognormal cumulative distribution (older name of LOGNORM.DIST).
fn.LOGNORM_INV: Inverse of the lognormal cumulative distribution.
fn.LOOKUP: Approximate lookup along a row or column.
fn.MAKEARRAY: Builds an array from a LAMBDA of the position.
fn.MAP: Applies a LAMBDA to every value, returning an array.
fn.MARGINOFERROR: Sampling error of a mean at a confidence level.
fn.MATCH: The position of a value in a range.
fn.MAXA: Largest value, counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.
fn.MAXIFS: Largest value among cells meeting several conditions.
fn.MDURATION: Modified duration of a bond: its price sensitivity to yield.
fn.MIDB: Characters from the middle (the same as MID here).
fn.MINA: Smallest value, counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.
fn.MINIFS: Smallest value among cells meeting several conditions.
fn.MINUTE: The minute of a time, 0 to 59.
fn.MODE_MULT: Every most-frequent value, as a column.
fn.MULTINOMIAL: Factorial of the sum over the product of the factorials.
fn.N: A value as a number: text is 0, TRUE is 1.
fn.NE: TRUE when the values differ (the <> operator).
fn.NEGBINOMDIST: Negative binomial distribution (older name of NEGBINOM.DIST).
fn.NEGBINOM_DIST: Negative binomial distribution: failures before the given successes.
fn.NETWORKDAYS_INTL: Working days with a custom weekend (1-17 or "0000011").
fn.NORMINV: Inverse of the normal cumulative distribution (older name of NORM.INV).
fn.NORMSDIST: Standard normal cumulative distribution (older name of NORM.S.DIST).
fn.NORMSINV: Inverse of the standard normal cumulative distribution (older name of NORM.S.INV).
fn.NORM_S_INV: Inverse of the standard normal distribution.
fn.NPV: Net present value of cash flows.
fn.NUMBERVALUE: Text to a number, with custom separators.
fn.ODD: Rounds up to an odd integer.
fn.ODDFPRICE: Price per 100 face value of a security with an odd (short or long) first period.
fn.ODDFYIELD: Yield of a security with an odd (short or long) first period.
fn.ODDLPRICE: Price per 100 face value of a security with an odd last period.
fn.ODDLYIELD: Yield of a security with an odd last period.
fn.OFFSET: A range shifted from a reference.
fn.OR: TRUE when any argument is true.
fn.PDURATION: Periods needed to reach a value.
fn.PEARSON: Pearson correlation coefficient of two ranges.
fn.PERCENTILE_EXC: Value at a percentile, 0 to 1 exclusive.
fn.PERCENTILE_INC: Value at a percentile, 0 to 1 inclusive.
fn.PERCENTOF: The sum of a subset as a share of the sum of everything; named in GROUPBY or PIVOTBY, each group's share of all the values.
fn.PERCENTRANK: Percent rank of a value in a list.
fn.PERCENTRANK_EXC: Percent rank of a value, exclusive of 0 and 1.
fn.PERCENTRANK_INC: Percent rank of a value, 0 to 1 inclusive.
fn.PHI: Density of the standard normal distribution at x.
fn.PHONETIC: The phonetic (furigana) text of a cell; #N/A where none is stored.
fn.PIVOTBY: A pivot: rows by one field, columns by another, each cell the function over the matching values, with totals.
fn.PMT: Payment per period for a loan.
fn.POWER: Raises a number to a power.
fn.PRICE: Price per 100 face value of a bond paying periodic interest.
fn.PRICEDISC: Price per 100 of a discounted security.
fn.PRICEMAT: Price per 100 face value of a security that pays interest at maturity.
fn.PROB: Probability that a value falls between the limits.
fn.QUARTILE_EXC: Value at a quartile, 1 to 3, exclusive of the ends.
fn.QUERY: Runs a Sheets-style query over the data: select, where, group by, order by, limit, label (e.g. "select A, sum(C) where B > 5 group by A").
fn.RAND: A random number from 0 up to 1, new at every calculation.
fn.RANDBETWEEN: A random whole number between two numbers.
fn.RANK: Position of a value in a list.
fn.RANK_AVG: Position of a number in a list; ties share their average rank.
fn.RANK_EQ: Position of a number in a list; ties share the top rank.
fn.RECEIVED: Amount received at maturity for a fully invested security.
fn.REDUCE: Folds an array into one value.
fn.REGEXEXTRACT: The first match (0), every match as a column (1) or the first match's groups as a row (2); left out, the capture group or groups if any. 1 ignores case.
fn.REGEXREPLACE: Replaces every match, or only the nth (counting from the end when negative).
fn.REGEXTEST: TRUE when the text matches the regular expression (1 ignores case).
fn.REPLACEB: Replaces characters at a position (the same as REPLACE here).
fn.REPT: Text repeated a number of times.
fn.RIGHTB: Characters from the end (the same as RIGHT here).
fn.ROMAN: A number as Roman numerals; form 0 or TRUE is classic, 1 to 3 more concise, 4 or FALSE simplified.
fn.ROUND: Rounds to a number of digits.
fn.ROWS: How many rows a range or array has.
fn.RSQ: R squared of the best-fit line.
fn.RTD: Data from a real-time data server program; none is available here (#N/A).
fn.SCAN: Like REDUCE, keeping every intermediate value.
fn.SEARCHB: Position of text, case-insensitive (the same as SEARCH here).
fn.SEC: Secant of an angle in radians.
fn.SECOND: The second of a time, 0 to 59.
fn.SEQUENCE: A block of counting numbers; spills.
fn.SIGN: 1 for a positive number, -1 for a negative one, 0 for zero.
fn.SIN: Sine of an angle in radians.
fn.SINGLE: The one value of a range on the formula's own row or column (the @ operator).
fn.SORT: Rows of a range in order; spills. A fourth argument alone is by_col (TRUE or 1 sorts the columns); more column and order pairs sort by more columns.
fn.SORTBY: Sorts the rows of a range by one or more other ranges (1 ascending, -1 descending).
fn.SPARKLINE: A tiny chart in the cell: "line", "column", "bar", or "winloss".
fn.SPLIT: Pieces of text in a row; spills.
fn.SQRTPI: Square root of a number times pi.
fn.STDEVA: Sample standard deviation counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.
fn.STDEVPA: Population standard deviation counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.
fn.STEYX: Standard error of the predicted y.
fn.STOCKHISTORY: Historical market data; needs a data service this app does not reach (#CONNECT!).
fn.SUBTOTAL: Aggregates visible rows only: 9 = SUM, 1 = AVERAGE, 3 = COUNTA, 109 also skips hidden rows.
fn.SUMIF: Adds cells that meet a condition.
fn.SUMPRODUCT: Sum of the products of matching cells.
fn.SUMX2MY2: Sum of the differences of the squares of matching values.
fn.SUMX2PY2: Sum of the sums of the squares of matching values.
fn.SUMXMY2: Sum of the squares of the differences of matching values.
fn.SWITCH: Matches an expression against a list.
fn.T: The value if it is text, otherwise empty text.
fn.TABLE: A What-If data table's formula, written by Data Table.
fn.TAKE: The first (or, negative, last) rows and columns.
fn.TAN: Tangent of an angle in radians.
fn.TBILLEQ: Bond-equivalent yield of a Treasury bill.
fn.TBILLPRICE: Price per 100 of a Treasury bill.
fn.TDIST: Student t distribution, one or two tails (older name of T.DIST.RT and T.DIST.2T).
fn.TEXTAFTER: Text after a delimiter; a negative instance counts from the end.
fn.TEXTBEFORE: Text before a delimiter; a negative instance counts from the end.
fn.TEXTSPLIT: Text cut into a block of cells by one or more delimiters; spills.
fn.TIMEVALUE: Turns time text into a time.
fn.TINV: Inverse of the two-tailed Student t distribution (older name of T.INV.2T).
fn.TOCOL: Flattens an array into one column (ignore: 1 blanks, 2 errors, 3 both).
fn.TOROW: Flattens an array into one row.
fn.TO_DOLLARS: A number as an amount of money (Sheets).
fn.TO_PURE_NUMBER: A value as a plain number, without its format (Sheets).
fn.TRANSLATE: Translates text with Puter AI (languages as codes or names; the target defaults to English). #BUSY! while it works.
fn.TRIMMEAN: Mean after dropping a fraction of the extremes.
fn.TRIMRANGE: The range without its blank leading and trailing rows and columns (0 none, 1 leading, 2 trailing, 3 both).
fn.TTEST: Probability from a t-test (older name of T.TEST).
fn.TYPE: The kind of a value: 1 number, 2 text, 4 logical, 16 error, 64 array.
fn.T_INV: Inverse of the left-tailed t distribution.
fn.T_INV_2T: Inverse of the two-tailed Student t distribution.
fn.T_TEST: Probability from a t-test: type 1 paired, 2 equal variance, 3 unequal.
fn.UNICHAR: The character for a Unicode code point.
fn.UNICODE: Code point of the first character.
fn.UNIQUE: Distinct rows (or columns) of a range; spills.
fn.VARA: Sample variance counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.
fn.VARPA: Population variance counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.
fn.VLOOKUP: Looks down the first column, returns from another.
fn.VSTACK: Stacks arrays on top of each other.
fn.WEBSERVICE: The text a web address returns; #BUSY! while it downloads.
fn.WEEKDAY: Day of the week as a number.
fn.WORKDAY: The date some working days away.
fn.WORKDAY_INTL: A working-days offset with a custom weekend.
fn.WRAPCOLS: Wraps a row or column into columns of a given length.
fn.WRAPROWS: Wraps a row or column into rows of a given length.
fn.XIRR: Rate of return with dated cash flows.
fn.XLOOKUP: Finds a value and returns its match; match_mode -1/1 takes the next smaller/larger, 2 allows wildcards.
fn.XMATCH: Position of a value: 0 exact, -1 next smaller, 1 next larger, 2 wildcard.
fn.XNPV: Net present value with dated cash flows.
fn.XOR: TRUE when an odd number of arguments are true.
fn.YEARFRAC: Fraction of a year between two dates.
fn.YIELD: Yield of a bond paying periodic interest, from its price.
fn.YIELDDISC: Annual yield of a discounted security.
fn.YIELDMAT: Yield of a security that pays interest at maturity.
fn.ZTEST: One-tailed probability of a z-test (older name of Z.TEST).
